content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity), Section 11.1 (p0187).**

**What the document does:** The Term is eight years (p0049). The sole Customer convenience exit requires (i) one full year's written notice and (ii) an early-termination fee equal to a redacted percentage of the "Estimated Remaining Value" — defined at p0039 as every remaining month of the Term multiplied by the Monthly Base Fee (or a higher three-month average) — stacked with unamortized Conversion costs and disposition Expenses, and expressly carved out of the Section 13.4 liability cap.

**Why it fails the fallback:** Both material terms miss. Notice is 12 months against a 60–90 day fallback; the fee is potentially years of fees against a three-month cap. This is a penalty, not a convenience right.

**Redline (validated ok:true), pitched at the fallback:**
- Notice: one year → **ninety (90) days**
- Fee: % of Estimated Remaining Value → **capped at 3× Monthly Base Fee**, payable once post-termination rather than 50% up front
- Added a **refund of prepaid Fees**; removed the disposition-Expenses add-on and the Section 13.4 carve-out
- Left M&I's **unamortized Conversion costs** recoverable — the up-front conversion investment in a core-processing outsourcing makes the preferred 30-day/no-fee position disproportionate here

**Noted, not flagged:** Section 10.2 (p0180) lets M&I withdraw non-Core Services at any time on 90 days' notice. That sits at, not below, the 90-day walk-away threshold and is mitigated by the good-faith Base Fee reduction in p0181, so I recorded it in the rationale rather than redlining it.
